faq.a: Gulnur is associated with the Arabic form غُولْنُور, whose core sense is gulnur; rose light (turkish).

faq.q: What is the origin of Gulnur?
faq.a: Gulnur is associated with Arabic. Gulnur is a Turkish compound of gül ('rose') + Arabic نُور (nūr, 'light').
Yes — the underlying form غُولْنُور is Arabic.
Gulnur can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Gulnur should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Nūr occurs in the Quran as a term for light.

faq.q: What does Gulnur mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Gulnur is rendered گل نور and carries the sense گل نور، گلاب کی روشنی.

faq.q: What does Gulnur mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Gulnur is rendered گلنور and carries the sense گلنور، نور گل.
A romanized syllable approximation is gul-nur. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Gulnur?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Gulnur, gulnur. Script forms are غُولْنُور, ګلنور, گل نور, گلنور, गुलनूर.

faq.q: Is Gulnur a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
